title: Governments, Civilians, and the Evolution of Insurgency: Modeling the Early Dynamics of Insurgencies
publisher: Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation (JASSS) 11(4) 7, by D. Scott Bennett

key_points.claim: Agent types and mechanism: civilians, insurgents and soldiers. Government counterattacks deter civilians through fear, but collateral damage angers them, and angry civilians become insurgents (agent internal states and behavior rules).
key_points.evidence_quote: If civilians become angry enough, they become new insurgents.

key_points.claim: Main finding: avoiding collateral damage matters more than capturing insurgents for long-term defeat of insurgency.
key_points.evidence_quote: accuracy (avoidance of collateral damage) is more important for the long-term defeat of insurgency than is effectiveness at capturing insurgents in any given counterattack.

key_points.claim: The model shows a tipping point in accuracy. Below it, insurgencies last much longer.
key_points.evidence_quote: There also may be a critical 'tipping point' for accuracy below which the length of insurgencies increases dramatically.

key_points.claim: Spatial structure: 2D bounded grid, local interaction within a Moore neighborhood, one agent per cell. A torus is an optional variant.
key_points.evidence_quote: By default, the grid is 50 x 50 cells. Each soldier or civilian in the simulation occupies one grid cell, and only one agent can occupy any cell location.

key_points.claim: Neighborhood and boundaries: agents interact only with neighbors within a Moore distance of 3 cells by default, on a grid with edge boundaries rather than a torus.
key_points.evidence_quote: agents interact only with their neighbors, where neighbors are defined as all actors within a specified Moore distance (3 cells by default).

key_points.claim: Empirical grounding: data on 129 insurgencies motivates a focus on the early stages.
key_points.evidence_quote: Bapat's (2005) data on 129 insurgencies since 1955 finds that while the mean duration of an insurgency is 7 years, the median is 4 years

key_points.claim: Design approach: minimal assumptions about agent interactions. The author cautions that real-world parameter values are uncertain, so extended insurgencies could result mainly from government actions.
key_points.evidence_quote: The simulation started with minimal assumptions about agent interactions

reliability_notes: Full text of a peer-reviewed JASSS article. I read the abstract, the space section and the conclusions, and searched the rest. The model is stylized and covers only insurgency, and the results are simulation-based with no empirical validation. Its relevance to the broader task is domain-specific (conflict and politics).
